_comment: Credit-trust band table shared by IDP (validator band_hint) and hydra (Ops decision runner, T07). Fable credit-trust design 2026-10-15: report.md section 3.4 + tickets T07/T11. hydra keeps a byte-identical mirror; tests/common/credit_trust_bands_parity_test.py compares the two. Change both in the same pair of PRs.

tiers._comment: Verifier design R1 (by Spotify popularity). IDP's big track (_is_big_track) = T2/T3: popularity >= big_track_popularity, a track artist >= big_artist_popularity, or an unknown popularity.

bands.A: auto-approve: the validator approved and the approval rests on trusted (non-muso) evidence: a trusted shortcut, or a score approval by a claimant with a trusted footprint
bands.B: request info: held or declined on evidence the claimant can supply (a high profile-level risk, big track without a trusted credit, weak footprint, risk >= approve_threshold), or approved on muso-only evidence / a weak footprint (audit, never band A)
bands.C: Ops decision: held for a reason the claimant cannot answer (trusted contradiction, account flags, velocity except an editing burst, Ops tombstone, a request racing an in-flight writer of the same pair, an auto-reject rule, an evaluation error)
bands.D: human only (never emitted by IDP): forged document on T2/T3, take-back on a paying account, T3 approvals, two escalations

evidence_bar._comment: Captain 2026-10-15 ~22:04Z: 'it should be very hard to get a high popularity track credit approved if the documentation is weak'. The bar scales with the tier. On T2/T3 an approval needs ALL of: a forensically genuine primary document naming the claimant in the claimed role, independent corroboration, and a footprint consistent with the role. Weak documents never count. Enforced by the deciding server (core T02/T12, hydra T07) with evidence_bar_missing(); IDP stamps the tier and the requirements on every claim.

high_risk_roles._comment: Captain 2026-10-15 ~23:42Z: 'also some abusers of editorial roles - we need this to be verified on high risk too'. Editing/editorial roles are easy to claim and rarely in public credits. A claimed credit is high-risk when its dict code matches code_pattern or one of its catalog roles is in catalog_children. Rules: never band A unless a trusted source credits the claimant in that role on the track (or its master); from documents_from_tier up a claim without that trusted credit is held for documents; a claim with a high-risk role runs at 1/velocity_weight of the velocity caps.

profile_risk._comment: Captain 2026-10-15 ~23:44Z: a holistic PROFILE-level (claimant) risk score, computed outside IDP (V2 ticket; core T02 kind=profile_review, board T03). Core sends it on the claim as content.profile_risk = {score, band, reasons, computed_at}; a band in hold_bands holds the claim under rule (docs required, no auto-approve). Absent or unparsable = no effect (the per-credit rules still apply).

proof_required._comment: Captain 2026-10-16 ~02:03Z: proof before approval is SCORE-DRIVEN for anyone, never a named-user list; no blanket or staff auto-approval. Every verdict carries proof_required + proof_required_reasons, consistent with band_hint: a proof ask exactly when a non-approval is band B. Band C (any band C rule fired or an evaluation error key, alone or layered under other holds) never asks the claimant: only Ops can clear it. Otherwise a non-approval asks when a rule in rules fired, an editing role was held by a velocity rule (editing_burst_rules -> reason editing_burst; that velocity hold is band B, not C), or the weighted score declined it (score_declined_reason).

org_roles._comment: Studio claims fraud check 2026-10-16: an organization role (Studio, Record Label, Publisher, Distributor, Recording Location, ...) claimed for a profile with NO outside (non-muso) source is held for proof (band B, never auto-approve): a claimant-minted org crediting itself on its own releases. A claimed credit is an org role when one of its catalog roles has a parent in catalog_parents or a child in catalog_children.

dedupe._comment: Studio claims fraud check 2026-10-16: a user request whose every (track, role) is already a live approved credit of the profile is a duplicate: it is reported APPROVED as a no-op (nothing written, no velocity slot, never a second credit), with rule at 0 and duplicate_of mapping each pair to the live raw credit id, logged [CREDIT_DEDUPE] (+24h fix-forward on IDP #1727: holding it left re-submissions of live credits 'unverified' for users). Only a request racing an in-flight writer of the same pair (credit not live yet) is HELD under rule (band C, no proof ask). A replay of the same request is recognised by request id (credit_request_approval) at any time.

hold_reasons._comment: Audit finding #8 (2026-10-16): every verdict that is not an approval stores hold_reason_codes (machine) and hold_reason (one plain sentence for the board and Ops). rules: the sentence for a hold/reject rule or an error key. scoring: the phrase for a weighted scoring rule, used when the score alone declined the claim ('{score}' and '{threshold}' are filled in). Every banded rule, error key and scoring rule must have text (parity test).

rules.reject_deleted_catalog_track: The track has been removed from the catalog.
rules.reject_high_risk_profile: The claimant's profile is flagged as high risk.
rules.reject_artist_credit: Artist credits are taken from the streaming services and cannot be claimed.
rules.reject_individual_org_credit: An organization role was claimed for a person's profile.
rules.reject_publisher_label_credit: Label and publisher credits come from MLC and Spotify data, so a new one needs Ops review.
rules.review_role_credited_to_other_at_trusted: A trusted source credits this one-person role on the track to someone else.
rules.review_big_track_weak_footprint: A popular track was claimed by a profile with no trusted credit in this role on any track, no verified streaming identity, and no ownership of the release.
rules.review_org_role_without_outside_source: An organization role (studio, label, publisher) was claimed for a profile that exists only on Muso, with no outside source.
rules.review_editing_role_without_trusted_cred: An editing role was claimed on a mid-size or popular track with no trusted source naming the claimant as an editor there.
rules.review_big_track_without_trusted_credit: A popular track was claimed with no trusted source crediting the claimant in this role on the track.
rules.review_high_velocity_profile: Too many claims on popular tracks were approved for this profile in the last 24 hours.
rules.review_hourly_velocity_profile: Too many claims were approved for this profile in the last hour.
rules.review_held_submitter: The submitting account is on the credit hold list.
rules.review_high_risk_profile_score: The claimant's overall profile risk score is high.
rules.review_operations_tombstone: Muso Operations removed this credit earlier, so it cannot be re-added automatically.
rules.review_duplicate_of_approved_credit: Another request for the same credit on this profile is already being processed.
rules.validation_error: The claim could not be checked because of a processing error.
rules._hold_on_error: A required check could not be completed, so the claim is held.
rules._no_signal: No scoring check had enough data to score the claim.
rules.profile_not_in_catalog: The claimed profile was not found in the catalog.
rules.track_not_in_catalog: The claimed track was not found in the catalog.
rules.track_pending_capture: The track is still being imported from the streaming service.
rules.missing_recording_ids: The request did not name a track.

hold_reasons.score_only_sentence: The risk score is {score} (approval needs under {threshold}){drivers}.

scoring.popularity: the track is far more popular than the claimant's profile
scoring.release_date: the track's release date is far outside the claimant's known career
scoring.collaborations: the claimant has not worked with these artists or collaborators before
scoring.profile_credit: the claimant rarely or never holds this role on other tracks
scoring.track_credit: the role is a high-risk one, or the track already has someone in this one-person role
scoring.track_artists_popularity: the track's artists are far more popular than the claimant's profile
